newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: London-based dollar selling coupled with local exporter interest helped the rand firmer on Tuesday, bringing its gains to almost four cents this week.
At the local close, the rand was pegged at 4.6360/6410 against the dollar from 4.6550/6600 at Monday's close and 4.6710/4.6760 on Friday.
Dealers said the rand began the day buoyed by a spillover of London-based dollar selling from Monday afternoon.
They said the offshore selling appeared to be linked to stale longs cutting their positions because of rising carry costs.
"A few of the stale longs are being shaken out...it starts getting expensive to have longs if the rand doesn't go anywhere," a dealer said.
Dealers said they had seen some stop losses triggered on the way down, which encouraged further dollar selling.
One trader also said local exporter selling contributed to the local currency's gains on the day.
"We've seen exporter dollars from the local corporates and a bit from offshore," she said.
Dealers said that a convincing breach of the 4.64 level could bring the 4.60 level into range.
"At the moment 4.64 is a bit of an importer level, but if we break it we could to the lower 4.60s," one said, adding that further stop losses were expected to be triggered on the way down.
The rand also managed to gain some ground against the pound, settling at 7.7585/7715 from 7.7711/7818 on Monday and at 0.3237/3242 marks from 0.3229/3234 previously.
Bond yields ended a languid day slightly higher as the market consolidated Monday's heady gains.
The key R150 settled at 15.865 percent from 15.84 percent overnight after touching a high of 15.90 percent.
"It has been a very quiet day," a dealer said, "and a little bit disappointing. After yesterday's move I expected a bit more."
Bond yields eased 16 basis points on Monday.

"The only interest we saw was local professionals. When they saw it wasn't coming down they started selling. We saw a bit of demand around 15.85 to 15.87 and then they tried to push it up to 15.90. That didn't work and here we sit," the dealer said.
Institutional orders had been few and far between on the day, he added.
On the money market, rates held steady despite another rise in the daily shortage.
The Reserve Bank said the daily shortage rose to 9.064 billion rand on Monday after dipping to 8.745 billion rand on Saturday from 8.8 billion rand on Friday.

The "big four" banks kept their three-month NCD rates steady at between 16.95 and 17.00 percent offered and 17.10 to 17.20 percent bid, while the 90-day BA rate was steady at between 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 123.88 million rand worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling a net 174.55 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes eased to 4.87 billion rand on Monday from 7.7 billion rand on Friday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
